problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}.$
